verdict: Tractor Supply's sales rose 5% to $3.9B on new stores, but higher transport costs and price investments squeezed margins, so profit fell 13% to $225M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net sales $3.91B vs $3.72B a year ago

kpis.label: Comparable store sales
kpis.note: vs +3.9% a year ago; improved through the quarter

segments.name: Rural lifestyle retail
segments.note: Sales from 2,486 Tractor Supply stores and 135 Petsense stores, plus Allivet and VIP Petcare — farm, pet, equine and home products for rural living. Tractor Supply reports one retail business, so this is its single revenue line, up 5.1%.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, distribution centers and head office — the company's biggest running cost.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, equipment and systems over their useful lives.

takeaways.title: Growth came from new stores
takeaways.text: Net sales rose to $3,910M, driven by 23 new Tractor Supply stores opened in the quarter, the VIP Petcare acquisition, and comparable sales up just 0.4% — new stores did most of the work.

takeaways.title: Margins were squeezed
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell a full point to 36.4% on higher transportation and fuel costs and deliberate price investments, while SG&A rose to 28.6% of sales, including startup costs for a new distribution center.

takeaways.title: Profit fell despite higher sales
takeaways.text: Operating income fell 10% to $308M and net income fell 13% to $225M. The company still returned $213M to shareholders — $89M of buybacks and $125M of dividends.

oneTimers: Tractor Supply closed 74 Petsense by Tractor Supply stores in the quarter, as previously announced; the related impairment charges ($63M over the first nine months) were recorded earlier in the year, not in Q3.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $19M — the cost of the company's borrowings, net of interest earned.
